newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks spiritual succor on eve of ceremony.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks spiritual succor on eve of ceremony.

text.p: President Bill Clinton sought spiritual inspiration by attending two church services on Sunday, on the eve of his inauguration to a second four-year term as the most powerful man on Earth.
Clinton and his wife Hillary began the day bright and early by driving across the Potomac River to the Columbia Baptist Church in the Virginia suburb of Falls Church.
The guest preacher was Pastor Rex Horne of the Immanuel Baptist Church in Little Rock, Arkansas, where Clinton was a regular worshipper before he became president in 1993.
Horne's theme was the need of Christians to submit to authority and respect the government as a divine institution. He exhorted parishioners to honour and pray for Clinton.
The first couple then proceeded to their usual Washington place of worship, the Foundry United Methodist Church, for a second dose of moral uplift.
He was met there by around 50 anti-abortion demonstrators holding large, gruesome pictures of bloody foetuses and a handful of people demonstrating against homosexuality.

Clinton, whose public approval ratings were soaring above the 60 percent mark, later delivered some brief remarks to the Democratic National Committee, whose members were meeting at a Washington hotel.

"I see the pictures of all the thousands and thousands of people in the shivering cold who were out on the Mall yesterday, all the children taking in the exhibits, and sensed the freedom and the feeling and the enthusiasm in the streets -- maybe this will be better the second time around," he said.
Clinton said that even when his political fortunes were at a low ebb in 1994 and 1995, he always believed he would win a second term.

"I've run my last race, but we haven't done all the work we need to do for our country, for the 21st century. We have to maintain both a commitment to progress and a commitment to community," he said.
The Clintons were scheduled to end the day with Vice President Al Gore and his wife Tipper at a star-studded Presidential Gala.

Clinton will take the oath of office at noon (1700 GMT) on Monday on the steps of the U.S. Capitol, the 53rd time the ceremony has been enacted. Aides said he was still working on the speech he will deliver to an expectant nation.
After several days of cruel, bone chilling cold, the Washington weather seemed to be smiling on the inauguration with temperatures forecast to rise above the freezing point on Monday.
In a Washington Post interview, Clinton said one of his themes would be the need to heal the deep divisions that have developed between Republicans and Democrats in recent years.
"I hope that I can set a tone Monday and in the days ahead that will help flush the poison out of the atmosphere and get people thinking about the folks that sent us all here," the president said.

Clinton, who faces numerous investigations into his business, political and private affairs in the months ahead, said politicians were devoting a disproportionate amount of time investigating alleged scandals, which took a huge amount of emotional energy from all involved.

"All of us, we have so little time and it passes so fast and we can do so much when we work together and think about the interests of the people and the future," he said. "It's a shame to waste this time by giving any more attention to these things than we need to."
History shows that while some inaugural speeches produced memorable and historic lines, most have been replete with cliches and have quickly been forgotten.

While Clinton focused on his message, the inauguration was an excuse for a huge party for thousands of Americans. Many braved the cold over the weekend to attend "An American Journey" festival on the Mall of Washington monuments.

Washington Post writer Joel Achenbach said there were two kinds of inauguration events: "Horribly crowded, free events held in unheated tents amid an Arctic windstorm (and) glitzy, elegant parties to which you are not invited."

For the nation's glitterati, the prime events were 15 inaugural balls scheduled for Monday evening. The president will put in an appearance at each of them on a day that will not end for him until the pre-dawn hours of Tuesday.
